Class IuValidator

java.lang.Object
edu.iu.validation.IuValidator
public final class IuValidator extends Object
Validates a business object against the Jakarta Validation constraints declared on its bean properties.

Every constraint on every reachable property is evaluated; nothing short-circuits. validate(Class, Object) returns the complete IuValidationResult so a caller can log or transform it; require(Class, Object) throws instead, for a service entry point that should reject bad input outright. 

IuValidator.require(EnrlHeader.class, header);

The object graph is traversed breadth-first from the root, so an arbitrarily deep graph costs heap rather than stack. A bean is validated at most once per pass, identified by instance identity: this terminates cycles, and means a single object reachable by two paths is reported under whichever path is reached first.

  • Method Details

    • validate

      public static <T> IuValidationResult validate(Class<T> type, T value)
      Validates a business object against the constraints declared by a specific type.

      Constraints are collected from the object's runtime class and its entire supertype hierarchy, which includes type. Passing type therefore does not narrow what is validated; it names the type reported by IuValidationResult.rootType().

      Type Parameters:
      T - business type
      Parameters:
      type - business type to report as the root of the pass
      value - instance of T; a null value has no properties to validate and is reported valid
      Returns:
      validation result; valid when no constraint failed
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if type is null

    • validate

      public static IuValidationResult validate(AnnotatedElement element, Object value)
      Validates one value against the constraints declared on an annotation target.

      For validating a value the caller already holds — a field, the return value of a getter, a method argument — where there is no bean to walk from. The target supplies the rules; the value is passed in. 

      IuValidator.require(parameter, argument);

      A Class target is validated as a bean, exactly as validate(Class, Object) does. Note that Class is itself an AnnotatedElement, so for a statically typed call such as validate(Foo.class, foo) the compiler selects validate(Class, Object) as the more specific overload; where it cannot, it selects this method, which delegates. Both routes therefore behave identically.

      Violation paths are rooted at the target's name: a Field reports its own name, a Method reports the bean property it reads if it is a getter and its own name otherwise, and a Parameter reports Parameter.getName(). That last is arg0 unless the declaring code was compiled with -parameters, so prefer validate(AnnotatedElement, String, Object) wherever a better name is available — from a jakarta.ws.rs.QueryParam, for instance.

      Parameters:
      element - annotation target: a Class, Field, Method, or Parameter
      value - value declared by element; may be null
      Returns:
      validation result; valid when no constraint failed, and when element declares none
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if element is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if element is any other kind of annotation target, such as a Constructor, Package, Module, or AnnotatedType

    • validate

      public static IuValidationResult validate(AnnotatedElement element, String name, Object value)
      Validates one value against the constraints declared on an annotation target, naming it explicitly.

      Use this wherever the caller knows a better name than reflection does. A REST dispatcher reading @QueryParam("message") can report message rather than arg0, and a cascading target then reports message.street.

      For a Class target, name roots every path of the bean walk, so a request entity validated as "body" reports body.emplid.

      Parameters:
      element - annotation target: a Class, Field, Method, or Parameter
      name - name to root the violation path at
      value - value declared by element; may be null
      Returns:
      validation result; valid when no constraint failed, and when element declares none
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if element or name is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if element is not a supported annotation target
